brief.headline: Push price to ₹0.65–0.80/pc (market says ₹0.85–0.95 is typical, so room exists at higher volume) and offer 15-day payment for a cut worth the early-pay value.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for pricing in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range for the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap at our volumes.
priceAsk.basis: The open market quotes ₹0.85–0.95/pc as typical, with a verdict of 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — we buy ₹44.37 L a year, so we should see that volume floor.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier (net 15 days after receipt instead of 30) in return for a price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹1.82 L in cash on hand — they should split that benefit with us as a price reduction.

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we can't tell how healthy or cash-tight they are. Our ₹44.37 L annual spend is material for a private converter, but without their revenue we don't know the exact weight. That means we lean on market data and the credible second sources we have lined up: Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, health score 65/100) and Mold-Tek (₹1010.97 Cr listed, health score 73/100) are both strong alternates for bottles and closures. The plan is to push firmly on price and payment using the market benchmark and the threat of qualifying one of those backups, but stay ready to walk if they won't move — we have options.

evidence.point: We spend ₹44.37 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging.
The market ask for a 28 mm PP cap is typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask band, ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, verdict 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec'

evidence.point: We currently pay 30 days after receipt; moving to net 15 days ties up ₹1.82 L of our cash.
HDPE resin import price is 87.61 ₹/kg — a proxy for raw-material cost movement.
Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) is a strong second-source candidate for pharma bottles and caps.
Mold-Tek Packaging (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health score 73/100) is another robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) with deep pharma capability in bottles, caps and preforms — top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health score 73/100) serving pharma with pails, containers, bottles and closures — strong and profitable alternate.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): manufacturer of rigid plastics, India-wide reach, medium confidence — could be a resin or finished-goods source.

risks: Rachana publishes no financials, so we're flying blind on their cash position and stability — watch for any signs of delivery trouble or quality slip that might flag distress.
We have no internal price benchmark (no 'best price we pay' figure) — rely entirely on the market ask and be ready to RFQ Manjushree or Mold-Tek if Rachana won't budge.
The market backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, etc.) are unqualified — treat them as research leads, not approved alternates, until we audit and price them.
If we push for ₹0.65–0.80 and they cite tight raw-material costs (HDPE at 87.61 ₹/kg), counter with the market verdict that ₹0.85–0.95 already has headroom built in at volume.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing our rigid-packaging supply base this quarter — market data shows typical pricing at ₹0.85–0.95 per piece with room to ₹0.65–0.80 at our volumes, and we've shortlisted Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources, so let's talk about where you can land on price and whether faster payment helps you.
